help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Despite rising turnover, profit fell; the return was below the interest rate.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The economy is weakening, demand is falling – and the investors’ return along with it.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Der Umsatz is everything that comes in before costs; der Gewinn is what is left after them, so it cannot be large if almost nothing remained.
help.tips[0].en.text: der Umsatz (turnover, all revenue) · der Gewinn (profit) · die Rendite (return on capital, in %) · der Ertrag (yield, earnings) · der Zinssatz (interest rate) · die Konjunktur (cycle: sich erholen, sich abschwächen) · die Nachfrage (demand: steigen, sinken) · die Insolvenz (anmelden).
help.tips[0].en.title: Economy: the money words that look alike
help.tips[0].en.trap: der Vergleich in law is a settlement, not a comparison; die Berufung is an appeal, not a vocation (though it is also that); der Einspruch is an objection to an administrative decision, not 'a speech'.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: She lodged an objection to the decision; in court a settlement was eventually reached.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The judgment is not yet final; the group has appealed.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Against a court judgment you go in Berufung to a higher court; Einspruch is against an administrative decision, and a Vergleich is a settlement.
help.tips[1].en.text: das Gesetz (parliament: verabschieden, erlassen) · die Verordnung (the executive: erlassen) · die Vorschrift (a rule) · Einspruch / Widerspruch einlegen gegen (object to an administrative decision) · in Berufung gehen, Berufung einlegen (appeal a judgment; Revision = appeal on points of law) · einen Vergleich schließen (settle) · Klage einreichen / erheben (sue) · ein Urteil fällen (rule); das Urteil wird rechtskräftig (becomes final).
help.tips[1].en.title: Law: act, regulation, rule; objection, appeal, settlement

help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The creditors asserted their claims; the supplier is liable for the damage.

help.tips[3].examples[1].en: High turnover, small profit, meagre return – the typical picture in retail.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: Umsatz minus Kosten = Gewinn; only expressed as a percentage of the capital would it become the Rendite.
help.tips[3].en.text: Turnover is everything that comes in; profit is what's left; return is profit as a percentage of capital. Three nested circles.
help.tips[3].en.title: Umsatz > Gewinn > Rendite
help.context.en: The economy recovered slightly in the third quarter, but inflation remains high; the central bank is therefore unlikely to cut the key rate. On the stock exchange shares reacted cautiously. Several medium-sized firms had to file for insolvency, while the unions are demanding higher wages in the collective bargaining round. Meanwhile the government issued a regulation on the platform economy; an industry association announced it would bring an action against it – a settlement is nevertheless considered likely.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: Umsatz is turnover; profit is Gewinn.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: Parliament passes (and issues) Gesetze; the executive issues Verordnungen. Both verbs exist; the subject is what matters.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: Einspruch / Widerspruch against an administrative decision; Berufung against a court judgment.
help.hookEn: Turnover, profit, return; objection, appeal, settlement — master the business-page words that look alike but never mean the same.
help.introEn: Economics and law supply the specialist register of the business and politics pages, and their vocabulary is precise in a way general German is not. Economy: die Konjunktur (the business cycle — Hochkonjunktur, Rezession), die Nachfrage / das Angebot, der Umsatz (turnover) vs der Gewinn (profit) vs die Rendite (return), die Inflation / die Teuerung, der Leitzins (key rate) and der Zinssatz, die Börse, die Insolvenz (Insolvenz anmelden), die Gewerkschaft, der Tarifvertrag, die Fusion (merger), das Kartellamt. Law: das Gesetz (act, passed by parliament: verabschieden / erlassen) vs die Verordnung (regulation, issued by the executive: erlassen), der Vertrag, das Gericht, der Einspruch / Widerspruch (objection to an administrative decision) vs die Berufung / Revision (appeal to a higher court), der Vergleich (settlement — not ‘comparison’ here), die Klage, das Urteil (rechtskräftig = final), die Frist, die Haftung (liability), die Forderung (claim), die Steuerhinterziehung. The verbs are fixed: Insolvenz anmelden, Einspruch einlegen, in Berufung gehen, eine Klage einreichen, einen Vergleich schließen, den Leitzins anheben / senken, die Nachfrage ankurbeln, für etwas haften.
help.rememberEn[0]: Umsatz / Gewinn / Rendite; Gesetz / Verordnung / Vorschrift; Einspruch / Berufung / Vergleich.
help.rememberEn[1]: Each noun has its verb: verabschieden, erlassen, anmelden, einlegen, schließen, fällen.
sentences[0].whyEn: die Rezession — two negative quarters is the classic definition.
sentences[1].whyEn: die Konjunktur — the economy's ups and downs.
sentences[2].whyEn: die Rendite — the return on invested capital.
sentences[3].whyEn: Insolvenz anmelden — the fixed formula for going broke.
sentences[4].whyEn: Einspruch einlegen — against official decisions; in court it would be Berufung.
sentences[5].whyEn: in Berufung gehen — the next judicial instance.
sentences[6].whyEn: der Vergleich — legally a settlement, not a comparison.
sentences[7].whyEn: der Leitzins — the rate that 'leads' all others.
sentences[8].whyEn: die Verordnung — issued by the executive, not a parliamentary law.
sentences[9].whyEn: der Tarifvertrag — the collective wage agreement.
sentences[11].whyEn: die Steuerhinterziehung — 'dragging taxes behind one's back'.
sentences[12].whyEn: die Forderungen — what one is owed; geltend machen is the formula.
sentences[13].whyEn: haften FÜR + accusative — to be legally liable.
sentences[14].whyEn: rechtskräftig — law + force: no longer contestable.
sentences[15].whyEn: die Inflation — the general price level rising.
sentences[16].whyEn: die Nachfrage — demand, supply's counterpart; ankurbeln like cranking an engine.
sentences[17].whyEn: der Verlust — the opposite of profit.
